extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in number theory/arithmetic geometry familiar with Mochizuki's IUT framework
extracted.subtask_description: Technical criteria, assumptions and inequalities used in Yamashita's exposition of an IUT-based approach to the abc conjecture; includes height-comparisons, local/global reduction hypotheses, choices of auxiliary primes, and anabelian reconstruction statements. Intended for checking applicability of lemmas/propositions and for following the reduction to initial data in the IUT framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: semistable reduction assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: E an elliptic curve over a number field F such that E has everywhere at most semistable reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a standing assumption in Lemma 1.13 and subsequent arguments; required for applying relations between various heights and for controlling q-parameters at non-Archimedean places.

rubrics_metrics.name: prime l and cyclic subgroup assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Let l > 2 be a prime, and H ⊂ E[l] a cyclic subgroup scheme of order l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline hypothesis for Lemma 1.13 and for constructing l-isogenies/quotients E → E/H and comparing heights; many arguments choose l satisfying further properties (P1)-(P7).

rubrics_metrics.name: height comparison: ht_!P1(f0;1;1g) vs ht_Falt (Lemma 1.13 (1))
rubrics_metrics.description: On UP1(Q) one has inequalities 2 ht_Falt . ht_!P1(f0;1;1g) . 2 ht_Falt + log(ht_!P1(f0;1;1g)) . 2 ht_Falt + ε ht_!P1(f0;1;1g) for any ε > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relates the line-bundle height coming from the Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism to Faltings height; the Archimedean contribution is controlled by compactness of the arc part and the non-Archimedean contribution has logarithmic singularities at {0,1,∞}. The final 'ε' form is used to absorb logarithmic terms in later bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: height change under l-isogeny (Lemma 1.13 (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Relation between ht_Falt([E;α]) and ht_Falt([E/H;Im(α)]): roughly ht_Falt([E/H;Im(α)]) is within ±(1/2) log l of ht_Falt([E;α]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comes from comparison of non-Archimedean and Archimedean contributions and cokernel bounds (cokernel killed by l). Used to control how heights shift under quotienting by an l-cyclic subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: non-Archimedean height behaviour under quotient (Lemma 1.13 (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A relationship between htnon_!P1(f0;1;1g)([E;α]) and htnon_!P1(f0;1;1g)([E/H;Im(α)]). If l is prime to v(q_{E,v}) for every v of bad reduction, then l · htnon_!P1([E;α]) = htnon_!P1([E/H;Im(α)]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires the additional arithmetic hypothesis that l does not divide the valuations of the Tate q-parameters at bad primes; used to obtain exact multiplicative relations for non-Archimedean contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: prime-to-q-parameter condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume l is prime to v(q_{E,v}) ∈ Z_{>0} for any v ∈ V(F) where E has bad reduction (for example, l > v(q_{E,v}) for such v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technical integrality/prime-to condition is invoked to identify canonical multiplicative subgroups in the Tate curve at local places and to deduce exact identities (see Lemma 1.13 (3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: global multiplicative subgroup implies bounded height (Corollary 1.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: If E[l] has a global multiplicative subgroup then the height of E is bounded: one gets an inequality of the form (l/(1+ε)) htnon_!P1([E;α]) ≤ ht_!P1([E;α]) + log l + C(ε) for some constant C(ε) independent of E,F,H,l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This corollary is used to rule out existence of global multiplicative subspaces for general E by finiteness arguments: existence would force bounded heights and hence finitely many isomorphism classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: interpretation/role of 'global multiplicative subgroup'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Global multiplicative subgroup' is a central concept in IUT: the corollary says such a subgroup (when global) forces bounded height of E, and IUT constructs analogous objects by 'going out of scheme theory' for sufficiently general E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is conceptual guidance rather than a technical inequality: it explains why the presence of such a subgroup is exceptional and motivates the use of IUT constructions in the main proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: q-parameter logarithm functions and equivalences
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of log(q8) and log(q-2): R-valued functions on the (j-)line obtained from normalized degrees determined by q-parameters at non-Archimedean primes (respectively excluding primes dividing 2l or excluding primes dividing 2). On compact K containing 2 one has log(q8) ≤ log(q-2), and  (1/6) log(q8) ≍ htnon_!P1 ≍ (1/6) ht_!P1 on K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare q-parameter sums with the non-Archimedean and global heights; these equivalences are invoked in the reduction to initial data and in bounding main terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diophantine inequality (Proposition 1.15)
rubrics_metrics.description:
For K ⊂ UP1(Q) compact (support containing the Archimedean place), A finite subset, and parameters d∈Z_{>0}, ε>0, there exists a finite exceptional set Exc such that for x ∈ (UP1(F)
K)
Exc with [F:Q]=d and various technical hypotheses, one has ht_!P1(f0;1;1g)(x) ≤ (1+ε)(log-diﬀ_{P1}(x) + log-cond_{f0;1;1g}(x)) + C_K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central Diophantine upper bound the paper reduces the main theorem to. The statement depends on many auxiliary hypotheses (models, torsion rationality, semistability, 'initial (2)-data' conditions) and allows enlarging Exc to exclude bad cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: rationality of low-order torsion and semistability (hypothesis for Prop 1.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume all points of E_F[3:5] are rational over F and that E_F^{tpd}[3:5] (model over F^{tpd}) is given by the Legendre form; also assume E_F has at most semistable reduction at all w ∈ V(F)_{non}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete hypotheses on torsion rationality and model choice are required to fit EF and its moduli/Ftpd into the 'initial (2)-data' framework; they are part of the finite-exception elimination strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: initial (2)-data SL2-image condition
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the 'initial (2)-data' it is required that the image of the outer homomorphism Gal(Q/F) → GL2(F_l) determined by E[l] contains SL2(F_l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This large-image condition is explicitly required in the definition of initial data and is enforced by choosing l with suitable monodromy properties (claims P2–P6). It is used to ensure the Galois representation is sufficiently non-degenerate to apply further IUT structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: finite exceptional set strategy (Exc_{K,d,ε})
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the reduction one enlarges a finite exceptional set Exc_{K,d,(ε)} (depending only on K,d,ε) to exclude finitely many 'bad' x so that the remaining x satisfy desired properties; Exc is changed only in ways depending on K,d,ε, not on x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard Diophantine/compactness device: remove a finite set of exceptional points that cause special degeneracies (e.g., low height, special automorphisms, unwanted torsion/subgroups).

rubrics_metrics.name: selection constraints for auxiliary prime l (P1–P3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constraints used to pick a large prime l not in a bad set A: (P1) an explicit upper bound control (used to ensure l is neither too small nor in certain ranges); (P2) l - h_v for all v with h_v ≠ 0 (monodromy non-vanishing modulo l); (P3) if l = p_v for some v then h_v < h^{1/2} (upper bound on monodromy at l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three properties are achieved by analytic/chebotarev-type counting and by excluding a finite set A of primes; they guarantee good reduction/monodromy behavior needed to build initial data and ensure SL2-image.

rubrics_metrics.name: exclude l-cyclic subgroup schemes (P4)
rubrics_metrics.description: By enlarging Exc one may assume that there does not exist any l-cyclic subgroup scheme in E_F[l].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is proved by applying Corollary 1.14: existence of such a subgroup would force bounded height and finitely many isomorphism classes, so after removing finitely many points one can assume none exist. This exclusion is used to force non-triangularity of Galois image.

rubrics_metrics.name: bad-multiplicative-reduction prime condition (P5)
rubrics_metrics.description: After enlarging Exc one may assume V_{bad}^{mod} ≠ ∅ and that for v ∈ V_{bad}^{mod} one has v ≠ 2l and E_F has bad multiplicative reduction at v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the existence of local places with multiplicative monodromy which are used to produce unipotent elements in the Galois image (e.g., N_+). If V_{bad}^{mod} were empty one obtains boundedness and finiteness and can discard those points.

rubrics_metrics.name: ensure large Galois image (P6)
rubrics_metrics.description: By the previous properties one can (after enlarging Exc) force that the image H of Gal(Q/F) → GL2(F_l) contains N_+ (upper unipotent), that H has more than one l-Sylow subgroup, and hence deduce H contains SL2(F_l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This monodromy/Sylow-subgroup argument ensures the required SL2-image condition for initial data. The combinatorial Sylow count (n_H ≡ 1 mod l) and the non-triangularity assumption are crucial.

rubrics_metrics.name: existence of appropriate initial (2)-data (P7)
rubrics_metrics.description: One may choose F,Q-data (F=F; X_F; l; C_K; V; V_{bad}^{mod}; ε) so that the resulting initial (2)-data satisfies the conditions listed in Section 1.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines P1–P6 to produce the exact data needed to apply Proposition 1.12 and the IUT machinery; this is the goal of the prime-selection and exceptional-set enlargement steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: anabelian reconstruction criteria for local fields (Proposition 2.1 (1)–(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an isomorphism φ: G_{K1} → G_{K2} of absolute Galois groups of finite extensions K_i of Q_p, one can reconstruct group-theoretically: (1) the prime p; (2) residue fields, valuation rings, and their inclusions via abelianization; (3) local degrees [K_i:Q_p], f(K_i), e(K_i); (4) inertia I_{K_i} and wild inertia P_{K_i} and their images; (5) Frobenius element preservation; (6) cyclotomic characters and Q/Z modules compatibility; (7) compatibility on H^2 classes coming from local class field theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are concrete anabelian 'reconstruction' standards: they specify exactly which local arithmetic objects are recoverable functorially from the profinite Galois group. The proof sketch explains group-theoretic constructions (abelianization, Verlangerung, coinvariants).

rubrics_metrics.name: group-theoretic characterisation of kernel for number fields (Prop 2.2 (1))
rubrics_metrics.description: In an exact sequence 1 → I → H → G → 1 with I topologically finitely generated and G = Gal(F^sep/F) for a number field F, the subgroup I is characterised in H as the maximal closed normal subgroup of H which is topologically finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the geometric kernel in arithmetic exact sequences purely group-theoretically and is used in anabelian arguments to detect the 'geometric' piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tamagawa criteria for p-adic arithmetic quotients (Prop 2.2 (Tam1),(Tam2))
rubrics_metrics.description: (Tam1) For every open subgroup H0 ⊂ H the coinvariant ((I0)^{ab})_{G0}/(tors) is a finitely generated free Z-module. (Tam2) For open subgroups H0 and every prime l ≠ p, the Q_p- and Q_l-dimensions of (H0)^{ab} scale with indices: dim_{Q_p}((H0)^{ab}⊗Q_p)/dim_{Q_p}((H)^{ab}⊗Q_p) = [(H):(H0)], and similarly for Q_l. Then I is group-theoretically characterised in H as the intersection of those open subgroups H0 satisfying (Tam2); p is characterised as the unique prime giving nonzero dimension for infinitely many l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These technical Tamagawa-type conditions allow one to recognise the geometric kernel in the p-adic (local) case by comparing abelianized dimensions across open subgroups; they are used to distinguish arithmetic vs geometric subgroups in profinite group extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tate-module coinvariants finite free (Lemma 2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a non-Archimedean local field F and a semi-abelian variety A over F, the module Q := T(A)^G/(tors) (T(A) = Hom(Q/Z, A(F))) is a finitely generated free Z-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to verify (Tam1)-type hypotheses: the G-invariant part of the Tate-module modulo torsion is a finite rank free Z-module because toric parts die on restriction and the abelian variety part yields finitely generated coinvariants by standard SGA and Tate module arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: miracle identity explaining main term 1 (Remark 1.15.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A combinatorial/equidistribution identity ('Miracle Identity') equates averaging factors coming from theta-functions and degrees (involving factors 1/(2l), degree 6 of (j- vs (222)-line), quadratic exponent of theta, linearity of terms, etc.), which yields the main term coefficient 1 in the Diophantine inequality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This conceptual identity explains why the leading coefficient of the inequality is exactly 1 and why it cannot be improved; it is not a technical hypothesis but a conceptual reason used to motivate the (2)-link and IUT constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: second-term exponent 1/2 behaviour and possible RH relation (Remark 1.15.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: An upper bound for the second main term of the Diophantine inequality on compact K is of the form constant + C · (log-diﬀ + log-cond)^{1/2} (exponent 1/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 1/2 exponent is noted to suggest a possible relation to the Riemann Hypothesis; references and comparisons to analytic number theory lower bounds (e.g., Masser) are given. This describes the expected size of the error/secondary term.

rubrics_metrics.name: uniform-abc dependence on degree parameter d (Remark 1.15.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit estimates are provided for the dependence of various constants and the exceptional set on the degree d = [F:Q], giving a quantified form of 'uniform abc' dependence (with explicit but complicated bounds involving d and auxiliary parameters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This entry records that the paper supplies explicit control of how constants and exceptional sets grow with the degree d; these formulas and the enlargement of Exc to depend on d are part of the program toward uniformity.
